# Preparation

This is the summary script for all basic descriptives of our project prior to the main analyses. 

```{r}
#| include: false
library(here)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(purrr)

source(here("scripts", "00_plotting_functions.R"))

# same filter and id padding as the Makefile
registry <- readr::read_tsv(here("data", "meta", "datasets.tsv"),
                            col_types = readr::cols(dataset_id = readr::col_character()),
                            show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(include %in% c("yes", "modify")) |>
  mutate(dataset_id = sprintf("%04d", as.integer(dataset_id)),
         label = paste0(first_author, " (", year, ")"))

features <- readRDS(here("output", "analysis", "features.rds"))

scale_bounds <- registry$dataset_id |>
  set_names() |>
  map(\(id) readRDS(here("data", "interim", paste0(id, ".rds")))$scale_bounds) |>
  bind_rows(.id = "dataset_id")

# item text is only kept in the raw openESM metadata, not in the interim files
item_text <- registry$dataset_id |>
  set_names() |>
  map(\(id) readRDS(here("data", "raw", paste0(id, ".rds")))$metadata$features[[1]] |>
        select(name, description, details)) |>
  bind_rows(.id = "dataset_id")

stopifnot(setequal(unique(scale_bounds$dataset_id), registry$dataset_id),
          setequal(unique(features$person$dataset_id), registry$dataset_id))
```

# Study design

```{r}
#| label: tbl-design
#| tbl-cap: "Study design per dataset."

registry |>
  arrange(first_author, year) |>
  select(label, n_days, n_beeps_per_day, n_time_points, sampling_scheme, lag_mode, topics) |>
  knitr::kable(col.names = c("Dataset", "Days", "Beeps per day", "Planned time points",
                             "Sampling scheme", "Lag mode", "Topics"))
```

# Items

We summarise the items per dataset. The mean and share at the bounds refer to the rescaled items. Items allowed outside their bounds can lie outside [0, 1], so their share at the bounds is not applicable (NA). SD and lag-1 autocorrelation (first training window) are medians over persons. Missing is the share of recorded rows without a response; beeps absent from the data (implicit missingness) are not counted, so this is a lower bound.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-items
#| tbl-cap: "Items per dataset. Mean and share at the bounds refer to the rescaled items. Items allowed outside their bounds can lie outside [0, 1], so their share at the bounds is not applicable (NA). SD and lag-1 autocorrelation (first training window) are medians over persons. Missing is the share of recorded rows without a response; beeps absent from the data (implicit missingness) are not counted, so this is a lower bound."

item_person <- features$item |>
  summarise(sd_median = median(sd_obs, na.rm = TRUE),
            rho1_median = median(rho1_train, na.rm = TRUE),
            prop_bound_mean = mean(prop_bound, na.rm = TRUE),
            .by = c(dataset_id, variable))

item_series <- features$series |>
  summarise(mean_rescaled = mean(y, na.rm = TRUE),
            pct_missing_recorded = 100 * mean(is.na(y)),
            .by = c(dataset_id, variable))

items <- scale_bounds |>
  rename(variable = name) |>
  inner_join(item_person, by = c("dataset_id", "variable")) |>
  inner_join(item_series, by = c("dataset_id", "variable")) |>
  left_join(mutate(item_text, in_metadata = TRUE), by = c("dataset_id", "variable" = "name")) |>
  mutate(prop_bound_mean = if_else(allow_outside, NA_real_, prop_bound_mean),
         composite = is.na(in_metadata),
         description = if_else(composite, "Composite (see modifier)", description))

stopifnot(nrow(items) == nrow(scale_bounds),
          nrow(items) == nrow(item_person),
          nrow(items) == nrow(item_series))

# composites are only added by modifiers, so items without metadata must come from such datasets
stopifnot(all(items$dataset_id[items$composite] %in%
                registry$dataset_id[registry$include == "modify"]))

items |>
  left_join(select(registry, dataset_id, label, first_author, year), by = "dataset_id") |>
  arrange(first_author, year) |>
  # a line break inside a cell ends the markdown table
  mutate(allow_outside = if_else(allow_outside, "yes", "no"),
         across(c(description, details), \(x) trimws(gsub("\\s*[\r\n]+\\s*", " ", x)))) |>
  select(label, variable, description, details, scale_min, scale_max, source, allow_outside,
         mean_rescaled, sd_median, rho1_median, prop_bound_mean, pct_missing_recorded) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2,
               col.names = c("Dataset", "Item", "Description", "Details", "Scale min",
                             "Scale max", "Bounds", "Outside allowed", "Mean", "SD, median",
                             "Lag-1 autocorr., median", "Share at bounds",
                             "% missing (recorded rows)"))
```

# Series length

Next, we plot the number of valid observations per person, by dataset. Valid observations are timepoints with complete responses and a usable lag, not all recorded rows. The point shows the median; thick and thin lines show the central 50% and 90% of persons.

```{r}
#| label: fig-series-length
#| fig-cap: "Valid observations per person, by dataset. Valid observations are timepoints with complete responses and a usable lag, not all recorded rows. Point: median; thick and thin lines: central 50% and 90% of persons."
#| fig-height: 7

series_length <- features$person |>
  left_join(select(registry, dataset_id, label), by = "dataset_id") |>
  mutate(label = reorder(label, n_valid, FUN = median))

stopifnot(!anyNA(series_length$label))

ggplot(series_length, aes(x = n_valid, y = label)) +
  ggdist::stat_halfeye(normalize = "groups", scale = 0.6, .width = c(0.5, 0.9),
                       fill = "#2C3E50", slab_alpha = 0.7, point_size = 2.5, colour = "#2C3E50") +
  labs(x = "Valid observations per person", y = NULL) +
  theme_bs()
```

# Missingness

```{r}
#| label: fig-missingness
#| fig-cap: "Share of missing item responses per person, by dataset, pooled over items and recorded rows. Beeps absent from the data (implicit missingness) are not counted, so this is a lower bound. Point: median; thick and thin lines: central 50% and 90% of persons."
#| fig-height: 7

missingness <- features$series |>
  summarise(pct_missing_recorded = 100 * mean(is.na(y)), .by = c(dataset_id, id)) |>
  left_join(select(registry, dataset_id, label), by = "dataset_id") |>
  mutate(label = reorder(label, pct_missing_recorded, FUN = median))

stopifnot(!anyNA(missingness$label))

ggplot(missingness, aes(x = pct_missing_recorded, y = label)) +
  ggdist::stat_halfeye(density = "bounded", normalize = "groups", scale = 0.6,
                       .width = c(0.5, 0.9), fill = "#2C3E50", slab_alpha = 0.7,
                       point_size = 2.5, colour = "#2C3E50") +
  labs(x = "Missing item responses per person (% of recorded rows)", y = NULL) +
  theme_bs()
```
